scope: Advice only against the frozen R1/R2 contract and profile. No production source, test source, catalog resource, real Vault, operator receipt, Git, network, or human-gate mutation was performed.

focus_areas.assessment: The thirteen closed groups, exact original document bytes, complete inventory, sorted keys, duplicate refusal, and derived coverage rows provide the intended closure. Implement validation must enforce cross-row foreign-key and cardinality identities rather than only per-row JSON shape.

R2 makes the retained current-basis and fixed-slot state machine explicit. Reconstruction, profile/resource/implementation/runtime binding, no-create status, exclusive install, complete-set checks, and final safety precedence are sufficient to reject self-consistent forged or foreign cache material when implemented as written.

Citation and display associations are separated for modern Markdown and legacy PDF/code resolution is exact-or-explicitly-unsupported. Legacy PDF charspan absence is correctly distinguished from malformed present spans. Keep the null legacy association fields and verify the complete artifact/parser/run/manifest ownership chain before any legacy result.

Registered-owned and registered-unclaimed sources, all artifacts including unreferenced material, and captured/derived coverage states are visible independently of cache state. No unclaimed source may be synthesized into a cited excerpt or hidden by lookup.

Exact identity lookup, frozen NFKC/casefold tokenizer, Han singles/bigrams, multiplicity, integer Dice score, positive-only hits, deterministic tie order, closed filters, and digest-bound paging are concrete. Freeze the boundary at which raw query limits versus normalized token limits are applied.
The contract explicitly preserves SOURCE_PROFILE_REQUIRED and exit75 at the legacy catalog_status boundary while keeping source-catalog envelopes and safety/history errors distinct.

findings.title: Make cross-row closure and evidence ordinal rules executable
findings.problem: The contract closes each row shape and says public code validates identities, but it does not enumerate the required foreign-key/cardinality checks. A producer could emit individually well-shaped rows with missing paper/source/association/display/head links, a claim without its declared assessment head, or evidence ordinals with gaps/reordered positions while still passing shallow schema validation.
findings.advice: Add contract tests and validator assertions: every referenced paper/repository/source/association/display decision/head exists; each claim has exactly one matching assessment_head and terminal event; every evidence group has unique zero-based original ordinals in source order; display-head and coverage references resolve; derived source_ids/paper_ids/repo_ids are exact sorted unique sets. Preserve malformed historical input as a typed error, never repair it in projection.
findings.required_test: A mixed fixture with missing foreign rows, duplicate or gapped evidence ordinals, wrong head hash, and mismatched derived sets must refuse with a specific ContractError before cache installation.

findings.title: Freeze raw-versus-normalized query bound semantics
findings.problem: The query limits are expressed in Unicode characters and UTF-8 bytes, while tokenization first applies NFKC and casefold. The contract does not say whether 512 characters/4096 bytes are checked on raw input, normalized text, or both; normalization can expand or alter length.
findings.advice: Specify that caller-supplied query UTF-8 bytes and Unicode character count are checked before normalization, then normalize/tokenize and apply the 1000-token bound to the resulting tokens; reject any normalized representation that exceeds the same bounded policy if the implementation materializes it. Add expansion cases such as U+00DF casefold and compatibility characters near both limits.
findings.required_test: Query strings at raw char/byte limits whose NFKC/casefold form expands, plus a nonblank string that normalizes to zero tokens, must return deterministic bounded errors without IO.

findings.title: Define lifecycle and assessment provenance at every result boundary
findings.problem: Claims store reference and assessment fields and state that lifecycle comes from the reference and assessment from validated terminal history, while query results expose lifecycle/assessment. The contract does not spell out the rejection rule for missing or unknown reference lifecycle, absent terminal head, or a source excerpt whose owning claim history is invalid.
findings.advice: Require a validated reference lifecycle enum and exactly one validated terminal assessment head for every claim before projection. A source-excerpt hit must inherit those validated values and cannot be included when its owner history is missing/ambiguous; preserve the typed source/history error instead of defaulting to active/all. Add fixtures for retired references, assessment forks, missing heads, and unknown lifecycle values.
findings.required_test: The same claim with accepted/provisional/contested/unsupported/deprecated history and active/retired references must produce the frozen filter matrix; missing/ambiguous provenance must refuse build.

findings.title: Keep legacy PDF/code exactness tied to citation ownership
findings.problem: Legacy evidence rows intentionally have association_id=null, so their exact citation authority cannot be inferred from the modern display association. The PDF/code resolver requirements are exact, but an implementation could validate only a parser/manifest locator and omit the artifact/source ownership chain or accidentally use the selected display association.
findings.advice: For every legacy PDF/code result, require source_id, artifact_path/artifact_sha256, validated parser/run or manifest/capture ancestry, and matching source ownership from retained inventory before returning RESOLVED. Keep display_association_id informational; when the chain cannot be reconstructed, return the fixed unsupported reason with null excerpt/hash/position rather than a display-derived excerpt.
findings.required_test: Select/rollback a modern display association while resolving legacy PDF and code citations, then mutate or remove one ancestry node; the first case must retain exact legacy citation behavior and the second must refuse or return explicit unsupported, never resolve through display.

required_tests: Closed row foreign-key/cardinality/ordinal/derived-set fixture, including malformed historical state and no cache installation.
Current-basis forgery and fixed-slot R2 state-machine tests, including no-create status and foreign byte-identical appearance; preserve existing IO review matrix.
Modern Markdown plus selected/rollback display association with historical citation B still resolving against B.
Legacy PDF exact JSON Pointer/page/text/span/hash success, missing optional charspan unsupported, malformed span/hash mismatch evidence error, and code manifest line-slice hash/newline behavior.
Coverage fixture for registered owned/unclaimed, captured registered/unregistered, derived referenced/unreferenced, and unreferenced historical files.
Chinese Han singles/bigrams, NFKC/casefold expansion, duplicate term counts, zero-token query, stable ties, all filters, pagination and catalog digest binding.
Legacy catalog_status source-aware fixture retaining SOURCE_PROFILE_REQUIRED exit75 while source-catalog errors remain distinct.
decision_basis: No new semantic blocker is found in the frozen R1/R2 contract. SEM-001 and SEM-004 are implementation assertions required for a sound closed projection; SEM-002 is a small profile clarification; SEM-003 is a provenance validation assertion. Existing R2 IO and cache-forgery advice remains applicable and is not overwritten by this review.

implementation_boundary.allowed: This artifact only; no source/catalog/Git changes.
